liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (3 reviews): The explosion into The Other One is singled out as a standout moment; The Other One is described as twisting and running with intense force [13][14][17]
- **Dark Star** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this a monster Dark Star version; A tease of Playin' near the end of Dark Star, possibly the earliest extant riff [12][18]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat segues into something other than Rider, which the reviewer treasures [20]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight runs about half an hour [12]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer especially loves the St. Stephen into The Eleven sequence [15]
- **Cryptical Reprise** (1 review): Cryptical Reprise drops in from a very high, quiet point before detonating [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-04-15.aud.sbd-patch.komar.miller.31939.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 123 min; rated 2.29/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.miller.31435.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 16 songs; 122 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says Jerry's vocals and guitar sound great, and the bass is also well captured; Recording is excellent given the circumstances, with Jerry's guitar out front; Audience tape is surprisingly listenable for its era [11][12][13][15][17][20]
- **gd1969-04-15.aud.komar.miller.31523.flac16**: audience recording; 16 songs; 122 min; rated 3.89/5 by 9 [3]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.komar.31672.sbefail.flac16**: audience recording; 15 songs; 122 min [4]
- **gd69-04-15.sbd.cotsman.6288.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 30 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [8]. Said about its sound: Soundboard segment is a short fragment with okay sound quality [9]

## Around the show

- A woman can be heard talking throughout Dark Star on the hand-held audience recording [10]
- The Eleven cuts off at the end of the recording [2]
- The Eleven has a substantial cut, including part of the William Tell Bridge [4]
- The cut in Lovelight is minimal, and track-start cuts omit only a few notes [4]
- Venue was The Music Box in Omaha, Nebraska; a Herb Greene photo accompanies the page [26]
- Works as filler alongside the other soundboard from the same venue dated 2/2/69 [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-04-15.aud.sbd-patch.komar.miller.31939.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Aiwa hand-held microphone -> Master Reel (Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel) -> Alesis Masterlink 9600 -> Hard Drive -> CD [1]. Also: Morning Dew through Doin' That Rag patched in from a soundboard source via cassette and DAT; Digital transfer by Jeremy Garrett at Rainbow Music, Omaha, September 2005, from discs supplied by Scott Allan; Original tape was 2-track mono, 3 3/4 ips, with automatic volume control switched on [1]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.miller.31435.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Jeremy Garrett, Scott Allan and Charlie Miller; source: Audience: Aiwa hand-held Microphone [2]. Also: Taped by an audience member holding the microphone by hand throughout the show; Tape was 2-track mono at 3 3/4 ips, with automatic volume control on [2][10]
- **gd1969-04-15.aud.komar.miller.31523.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Aiwa hand-held microphone -> Master Reel (Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel) -> Alesis Masterlink 9600 -> Hard Drive -> CD [3]. Also: Digital transfer by Jeremy Garrett at Rainbow Music, Omaha, September 2005, from discs supplied by Scott Allan; A flaw in one DAT tape was fixed on November 15, 2005 [3]
- **gd69-04-15.aud.komar.31672.sbefail.flac16**: taped by Leon Komar; transferred by Bob Bihlmayer; source: portable Aiwa 5" reel-to-reel, stock Aiwa hand-held microphone; "Automatic Volume Control" (compressor/limiter?) switch ON. [4]. Also: Real-time transfer with flat EQ and no filters; source discs and equipment info came from Iver McLeod [4]
- **gd69-04-15.sbd.cotsman.6288.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [8]
